# A valid plateau construction from independent endpoint pairing

Let three consecutive integer fibers be A,B,D in R^d, with A,D having
positive volumes a,c and B containing (A+D)/2. Let X,Y be independent
uniform points of A,D, and let f denote the density of (X+Y)/2. Choose
0<r<=min(a,c), and define g=rf. For h>1 put

    J_h={x:g(x)>=h-1}.

When J_h has positive volume it is compact and convex. There exists a
target measure h 1_{J_h}(x) dx in the middle fiber such that its mass in
every closed ambient halfspace is bounded above by the original mixed
volume in that halfspace. In particular, if M is the original total
volume and h vol_d(J_h)>=M/2, the uniform probability measure on J_h is
dominated in every halfspace by twice normalized mixed volume.

Proof. The midpoint density is

    f(x)=2^d/(ac) vol_d(A intersect (2x-D)).

For x,y and 0<=lambda<=1, Minkowski interpolation gives

    (1-lambda)[A intersect (2x-D)]
      +lambda[A intersect (2y-D)]
      subset A intersect (2((1-lambda)x+lambda y)-D).

Brunn-Minkowski implies that f^{1/d} is concave on (A+D)/2. The
convolution of two integrable bounded compactly supported indicators is
continuous; this also follows directly by continuity of translations
in L^1. Thus its positive superlevel set J_h is compact and convex.

Give the independent endpoint coupling total mass r. Its two source
marginals have densities r/a on A and r/c on D, bounded by one.
Accept an output x in J_h with factor min(1,h/g(x)), and reject outputs
outside J_h. The accepted midpoint density is min(g,h) 1_{J_h}; both
source marginals remain bounded by their original fiber volumes.

Add central singleton outputs with density (h-g)_+ 1_{J_h}. This is at
most one because g>=h-1 on J_h, and J_h subset B. The combined target
density is exactly h 1_{J_h}. Each midpoint output in a closed halfspace
has a source in that halfspace, and each singleton is its own source.
Summing source measures proves the stated domination, including oblique
halfspaces and all closed boundaries.

This sufficient construction is not universal. If d=1 and A=B=D is an
interval of length a, the largest permissible pairing r=a gives
g(x)=2(1-2|x|/a) after centering that interval. For 1<h<=3,

    h |J_h|=(a/2)h(3-h)<=9a/8<3a/2=M/2.

Smaller r cannot improve any positive superlevel set. Thus independent
pairing alone fails even this equal-fiber product, although other
couplings do yield the desired uniform target there.
